test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 03 Sept, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Pipe P can fill (2)/(7) part of a tank in 18 hours, and pipe Q can fill (5)/(9) part of the same tank in 25 hours. Both P and Q were kept open for 3 hours, then both were closed. Pipe R alone was then opened and it emptied the water in the tank in 8 hours. Pipes P, Q and R together can fill the empty tank in:
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total time: **P** = 18 × (7/2) = 63 hr; **Q** = 25 × (9/5) = 45 hr.

LCM(63, 45) = **315 units** (Total Work). Efficiency: **P** = 5, **Q** = 7.

In 3 hours, **P+Q** fill (5+7) × 3 = 36 units. **R** empties 36 units in 8 hr → EffR = 4.5.

Combined Efficiency (P+Q−R) = 12 − 4.5 = 7.5. Time = 315 ÷ 7.5 = 42 hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 42 hr.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** P fills 2/7 part in 18 hr; Q fills 5/9 part in 25 hr; R empties the 3-hour filled volume in 8 hr.

**Formula Used:** Total Work = Time × Efficiency

 
 

 
 **Person** **Days/Hr** **Total Work** **Efficiency** 

 Pipe P 63 315 5 

 Pipe Q 45 7 

⇒ Total work filled by **P and Q** in 3 hours = (5 + 7) × 3 = **36 units**.

⇒ Efficiency of **Pipe R** (Emptying) = Filled Volume ÷ Time = 36 ÷ 8 = **4.5 units/hr**.

⇒ Combined efficiency of **P, Q, and R** = 5 + 7 − 4.5 = **7.5 units/hr**.

⇒ Time taken by all three to fill the tank = 315 ÷ 7.5 = **42 hours**.

**∴ The correct answer is 42 hr.**

**__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns Sign Convention

Efficiency of an **inlet pipe** is taken as positive (+), while the efficiency of an **outlet (emptying) pipe** is taken as negative (−).

Fractional Work to Full Work

If a pipe fills 1/x part in t hours, it fills the full tank in **x × t** hours.

Combined Efficiency

Total Time = (Total Capacity) ÷ (Sum of efficiencies of all active pipes).</p
